items.note: The focused table filter keeps its 1px ink border and adds the pink halo band and an ink ring, and the narrowed one-row table stays ink-ruled under a lemon header band with black footer, close to the reference's chrome (06). The one off-system mark is the field's clear glyph, which is still a default blue, where the reference keeps every chrome icon ink.

Dark keeps the black ground with raised panels a step lighter, the white current nav pill and the pink search button, as the reference's dark capture (11) does. The focused filter shows a pink halo on the raised field with a white clear glyph, and the lemon band and periwinkle parcel stay unchanged. The footer now opens with a visible seam.

On a phone the header stacks the pill nav, the search row and the lemon band with the parcel cropped at the trailing edge, much like the reference's stacked phone chrome (10). The focused filter carries the same halo and ring. The two-column table below is cut at the frame with no scroll cue (agent layout, recorded on row hover).

The project table is one ink-framed white box on paper with a bold header row, 56px ruled rows, outline status pills with dots, and a notched pink flag in the budget cell. That is the reference's hairline frame language, and the read-only rows correctly gain no shading or lift on hover. Pink flags in every row stay loud, which the spec allows for one money cell per row.

In dark the table becomes a raised box with 35%-white rules on the black ground. Flags and status pills keep their light-mode fills, so depth reads the right way up as in the reference's dark capture. The rows correctly stay flat on hover.

The phone keeps the band, stacked stat tiles, chart and activity panels in the reference's ink-box language (10). The table, though, gives its first column about two thirds of the width, so the second column is cut mid-word at the frame and nothing shows that the table scrolls.

Keyboard focus on the sidebar's next nav item draws a 2px ink ring around a pill, beside the filled black current pill. This matches the reference's heavier ink focus outline (05) and keeps position (filled) distinct from focus (outlined).
In dark the focused nav item gets a white ring next to the white current pill. It stays clearly readable on the black sidebar and keeps the reference's swap of the current pill in dark (11).

In the phone's horizontal pill nav, the focused item gets a heavy ink ring pill that sits right against the black current pill. It reads clearly, but the row is tight: the last pill runs to the screen edge, where the reference keeps a gutter.

The account menu is a white ink panel with a static hard black shadow and a ruled header, over the lemon band, and the trigger is lifted. That is the reference's picked-up overlay (05). The account address in the menu header breaks mid-word onto a second line, which looks unfinished next to the clean reference panels.

In dark the menu is a raised dark panel over the lemon band, but its 35%-white offset shadow almost vanishes against lemon. The panel reads as a flat pasted box rather than the reference's lifted overlay. The rows and the ruled header are otherwise in the system.

On a phone the menu opens as a wide white ink panel with a hard black shadow over the band, with 48px-tall rows and a ruled header. It reads as a deliberate overlay in the reference's language. The address still wraps mid-word (recorded on desktop).

No results is a dashed white box holding a thick lemon magnifier sticker with a visible back strip, a one-line message, a muted hint and an outline clear action. It builds on the reference's dashed empty state (06) with the system's own drawing, and what to do next is obvious.
Dark keeps the dashed box on the raised tone, so the lemon magnifier sits on a raised field rather than the black ground, as the spec requires. The message and outline action read clearly.

On a phone the dashed empty box spans the column with the magnifier sticker at a healthy size, a two-line message and a centred outline action. It closely follows the reference's phone empty state (10).

Loading swaps the stat tiles for dashed raised placeholder boxes with visible loading text, and the band button shows a small stepped glyph with a refreshing label. There is no spinner or shimmer, just the drawn, flat placeholder language the spec derives from the reference's dashed boxes.

In dark the placeholders are dashed boxes on the raised tone with loading text, and the refreshing button stays white on the band. It is consistent with light, though the grey dashes are fainter than the reference's ink hairlines.

The phone shows four dashed placeholder tiles in a 2-up grid with loading text and the refreshing button in the band. It is clear and flat, in the same drawn register as the reference's phone empty state.

The overview band carries one periwinkle parcel sticker with ink inner seams and a label, cropped by the trailing edge only. Beside it is a chart drawn as a pink line over grey bars with ink caps. The parcel is a real object, but it reads thinner than the reference's coins, and its size sets a band twice as tall as the title block, so the lower half of the band is empty lemon.

The projects band holds a white ticket with a dashed tear line, side notches, ruled lines and a solid back strip, tilted on periwinkle. It is close to the reference's white paper stickers (03) in construction and weight, and it is its own object.

The item page uses a marigold folder with a tab, a label slot and a back strip, tilted and cropped by the band's right edge. It is a distinct noun drawn to the thick sticker recipe with an even ink outline, close to the reference's flat ink-outlined objects.

The team band shows a lemon ID badge with a clip slot, a solid ink photo square, ruled lines and an offset back on teal. It reads instantly as what it stands for, is different from the other screens' stickers, and has the chunky die-cut feel of the reference.

findings.summary: In dark mode the account menu over the lemon band loses its hard shadow: the 35%-white offset barely shows on lemon, so the menu reads as a flat pasted box. The reference's overlays always look picked up. The earlier verdict named this and it is still open.
The focused filter field's clear glyph is still the browser's default blue in light mode. The reference keeps every chrome icon ink. The earlier verdict named this too.

The overview header band is about 250px tall because of its sticker, while the title and lead fill only its top 100px, so the lower half is an empty lemon field. The parcel's side strip is also slimmer than the reference coins' rim. The reference's header bands (06) are tight around their content, and its stickers carry a deep solid edge.
The account address in the menu header breaks mid-word onto a second line, on desktop and on phones.

On phones the data table gives its first column about two thirds of the width. The next column is cut mid-word at the frame, and nothing shows that the table scrolls. The earlier verdict named this and it is still open.
